label: Early copy step (output orig[1]) in long sequences, upcoming h/f/b/z
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, never during the original input; 99% of mass is at copy steps. Concentrated at the first copy step after <DEL> (recall_idx==1, input = orig[0], output = orig[1]): 81% of mass, plus 18% at recall_idx 2 and a little on <DEL> itself. Rate rises sharply with L (L=9 holds 56% of mass). Within those steps it prefers sequences whose next outputs (orig[1] or orig[2]) are h, f, b or z (5-7x lift), and current input tokens 3, 2, y, t, p, q, b, c. The plain position predicate recall_idx==1 covers 81% of mass but has only 10% precision, so the token dependence is real but only partly captured. Highest activations are on inputs q, 3, c, b at step 10 (L=9). Does not fire at recall_idx >= 3 or in short sequences much.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the third original token (most: h, z, f, b, r, l; least: y, a, c, t) and the current input token, by step (t=11: 3, y, t, 2; t=12: y, 3, t, 2; t=10: 3, 2, t, y); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=1, L=9 & t=11, recall_idx=2.
